_notes: Declared by the skeleton from docs/design/office-design.md 1.2 (with decisions D4 and D11). Dimension 9's value office-ladder was added to the closed vocabulary by the skeleton (scripts/lib/fingerprint.ts, docs/design/research/spam.md).

human: one check per game (scripts/lib/fingerprint.ts reads human.<dimension> as a map keyed by the other game's id). value, by and date are all left empty on purpose: the person who looks writes the verdict ('own' for dimension 7, 'different' for 13; anything else counts as not differing), their name and the date, one entry per game (D9: an engineer's read is recorded as theirs; a read by the owner stays required before a submission). Until 'by' is filled the dimension reads pending. Dimension 7 waits for the icon and the 'signature' screenshot template (7.9) and SIDE-BY-SIDE.png; dimension 13 for the Ledger, the Cabinet photograph, the pinned ward map, the chalk tally board and the Office wall in the web preview.

24 November 2026, after the store review of the built game (screens lead): dimension 13 against Pizza Empire rested on the Ledger, which read as the first game's upgrade list; under D43 it is now a clothbound book (ruled lines, the storeys inked in the margin, the record as a running total, 'Raise' as an inked link, no filled price buttons, the ad card a slip tucked in the book) and it appears in no store image. Dimensions 11 and 12 score Jaccard 0 because each game names its own ids: ministers here are the same idea as Pizza Empire's managers and Lantern Row's minders, and prestige is shared; REVIEW-NOTES.md names that kinship openly. Dimension 17 against Lantern Row sat near the 5 % line: re-measure it (npx tsx scripts/validate.ts high-office) after every change to src/ui/decree/strings.ts. Dimension 8 stays pending until the lead runs npm run check:bundle -- --export after the last content write.
24 November 2026, the store step: what a person looks at before filling human.<dimension>.<game> (value 'own' for 7, 'different' for 13; by; date), with where the evidence is.

Dimension 7 (icon and screenshot template), evidence: games/high-office/store/screenshots/SIDE-BY-SIDE.png (the four games' icons, Play feature graphics and first three iPhone 6.9" shots, one row each), every set under games/<id>/store/screenshots/, the template code scripts/store/templates/signature.ts against warm.ts, panel.ts and tag.ts, and scripts/store/README.md's tables. Ours: the game full-bleed (no card, no frame, no tilt, nothing above it), a translucent baize band across the foot, the caption handwritten in slanted pale-violet nib capitals at the bottom left ending in a flourish and a pen nib; light icon (pale paper, violet signature, ribbon scissors).

Dimension 7 against pizza-empire: look whether the set reads as the same template as the warm cream frame (Pizza Empire frames the phone screen on a white-edged card leaning left and right on gingham, centred rounded headline plus a sub-line on a red sauce wave BELOW the game). Ours has no card and no sub-line, the caption sits ON the game at the left, in a hand, on green. Icons: Pizza Empire's warm illustrated tile against our pale paper with a violet stroke.

Dimension 7 against space-miner: look at the caption's place and type (Orbit Haulers: a hard-edged deep-blue readout panel ON TOP with monospaced capitals and a channel counter CH 01/06, the game below it edge to edge). Ours: no panel on top, no counter, no monospace; the nearest point is that both show the game edge to edge. Also the first caption: Orbit's first two are 'Drone to rock. Ore to hold.' and 'Swipe up. Freighter away.'; ours lead with the pull DOWN into the drawer ('Refused papers await further study'), the signing second, no clipped two-part captions. Icons: Orbit's navy tile against our light one.

Dimension 7 against night-market: look at the foot of the images (Lantern Row: the game fades into a dusk sky, a rice-paper tag hangs off-centre from a wire of lanterns, upright paper-cut capitals centred on the tag, tilted 3 degrees). Ours: no fade, no tag, no wire, no tilt; a straight band, slanted ink, left-aligned. The nearest point is that both captions are capitals drawn from each game's own art kit: judge whether paper-cut letters on a tag and nib lettering on a band read as one house style. Icons: Lantern Row's dusk tile against our light one.

Dimension 13 (meta screen layouts), evidence in the web preview (GAME=high-office, port 8303; switches in src/ui/decree/*/dev.web.ts): the Ledger (?preset=mid&sheet=ledger: a clothbound book, ruled rows, storeys inked in the margin, Raise as an inked link), the Cabinet photograph (&sheet=cabinet), the pinned ward map (&sheet=poll; store image 4), the chalk tally board (&night=play; store image 5), the Office wall (&wall=1; store image 6). Against pizza-empire look first at the Ledger beside Pizza Empire's upgrade list (D43: it read as that list before its rework; it is in no store image); against space-miner at the poll map beside the Star Map and the Contract Board; against night-market at the Office wall and the tally board beside the Ladder Book and the Lantern Gate.
